subject: Batch inference: request for temporary completion-window exception and idempotency guarantees
messages:
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-retail.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme-retail.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly batch SLA behavior and completion windows

Hi Marissa,

We're seeing intermittent overruns on our nightly batch inference jobs powered by Redwood: roughly 2-3 times per month a run that historically completed within 3 hours drifts past 6 hours and occasionally needs manual intervention. Our infra team flagged this as a compliance risk for our ingest SLAs and procurement wants clarity on whether Redwood can commit to a job completion window or provide a formal exception with compensating controls (retries, idempotency guarantees, and observable logs we can forward to our audit team).

Concretely: can Redwood provide a documented exception that covers our nightly 1.2M-record job with a guaranteed completion window (e.g., 6 hours) for a defined carveout period, plus details on retry behavior and a deterministic idempotency scheme so we can safely re-run without duplication? Also need to understand what monitoring/log retention you would provide for audit.

We're on a tight procurement timeline. Legal would like a written proposal they can attach to the SOW. CC'ing our legal address.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Nguyen
Head of ML Ops, Acme Retail
---
Attachment: run_samples_202607.csv (sample job manifest)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nightly batch SLA behavior and completion windows

Hi Tom — appreciate the context and the sample manifest.

Short answer: we can propose a time-limited completion-window exception with clear compensating controls (idempotency + structured retries + extended logging/retention) while we investigate the root cause for overruns. We need to validate a few workload specifics (effective tokenization, peak concurrency, and whether KV-cache warm starts are possible) before committing final language.

I'll loop in our SRE and platform engineering to draft a proposal legal can attach. Proposed next steps:
- Internal tech review (24–48 hrs) to confirm the 6-hour carveout is feasible for the provided job manifest.
- Draft an SLA addendum describing the exception window, retry semantics, idempotency scheme (job UUID + deterministic resume), and monitoring guarantees.
- Provide a temporary enhanced logging pipeline (48–72 hrs) to satisfy audit requests — we'll include retention details.

If that plan works, I'll follow up with a written proposal by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: dev.patel@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 13:26:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Nightly batch SLA behavior and completion windows — tech proposal

Team — quick internal notes after Marissa's ping and Tom's manifest: 

Summary of constraints:
- Nightly job size ~1.2M records, variable sequence lengths (avg 350 tokens), peak window 2–4 AM PT.
- Current failure mode appears to be resource contention at peak plus repeated retries that queue and extend total completion wall time.

Proposed carveout and controls (draft):
1) Completion window exception: guaranteed completion within 6 hours for nightly job runs for a 90-day carveout period, provided the job manifest and concurrency profile do not change by >15%.
2) Idempotency: require job-level UUID; server-side resume support keyed by UUID + deterministic offset checkpointing. Re-runs will not re-process already checkpointed records. We'll document the exact resume tokens and a recommended client-side backoff.
3) Retries: exponential backoff with max 3 attempts per chunk; chunk sizes configurable. We will ensure retries are idempotent by design (see #2).
4) Monitoring & logs: we will provision an audit stream for the customer's run with 90-day retention and include per-chunk latency histograms, retry counts, and final completion timestamps. We'll provide a CSV stub (SRE_run_windows.csv) showing the expected columns for audit export.
5) Credits & escalation: if a run exceeds 24 hours end-to-end, Redwood will issue a service credit equal to 5% of that month's inference usage for the account, pending approval from Finance.

Risks/Notes:
- We need to ensure the customer's network egress and client retries don't contravene our resume assumptions.
- This requires a small runtime change to persist deterministic resume tokens for async jobs (INF-4521). I filed a ticket and included a tentative ETA of 10 business days for the engineering work; the carveout can be effective immediately with the caveat that client must include a job UUID and we treat runs as eventual-resume without guaranteed partial-result streaming until the runtime change lands.

If everyone agrees, I'll draft the addendum language and Marissa can deliver to Acme legal.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Platform Engineering
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nightly batch SLA behavior and completion windows — proposed addendum

Tom — attaching our proposed addendum and a small SRE CSV describing the audit fields. Highlights: 6-hr completion window for nightly runs for 90 days, idempotent resume by job UUID, exponential retries (3 attempts), 90-day log retention, and a credit clause if a run exceeds 24 hours.

Attachment: idempotency-proposal-v1.md (text details)
Attachment: SRE_run_windows.csv (audit columns)

Are you able to confirm acceptance of the technical controls so legal can incorporate the addendum language? One ask from our side: please ensure the job manifest you send to the API includes a stable job UUID and chunk-size hint.

If accepted, I will route the addendum for signatures and trigger INF-4521 to prioritize the resume-token persistence work.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-retail.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nightly batch SLA behavior and completion windows — proposed addendum

Marissa, Aditya, Evelyn — thanks for the speedy turnaround. We reviewed the addendum and the controls look acceptable to Acme. Two quick clarifications before we sign: 
1) Can Redwood confirm that per-chunk retry records and completion timestamps will be available in the audit CSV we can pull (not just in internal logs)?
2) Our procurement requires 180-day retention for audit artifacts. Is that negotiable for the carveout period?

If you can confirm those two items in writing, procurement will attach the addendum to the SOW and we can move to signatures.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Nguyen
Head of ML Ops, Acme Retail
